newsitem.title: USA: AT&T, Hewlett-Packard in electronic commerce pact.
newsitem.headline: AT&T, Hewlett-Packard in electronic commerce pact.

text.p: Telecommunications giant AT&T Corp. and computer power Hewlett-Packard Co. said they agreed to an alliance designed to make it easier for companies to conduct business over the Internet via "electronic storefronts" and private networks.
Executives of the two companies said the pact would focus on developing products to make merchant use of electronic commerce easier through electronic communications and commerce services.
AT&T will provide services for secure purchases over the Internet and HP will provide computer systems, they said.

The telecommuncations company said it plans to recruit HP's nearly 15,000 resellers, or third-party marketers, as agents to sell AT&T's Web site services, such as Web hosting, which provides companies with Web sites on AT&T computers.
AT&T and HP said they will integrate their technologies to create electronic storefront systems, giving merchants the option to host a Web site with secure electronic commerce capabilities.

Executives of the two companies said the deal was not exclusive. But Glenn Osaka, general manager and vice president of HP's extended enterprise group, said the deal extends the companies' combined reach and ability to integrate products, while accelerating the speed of market adaption.
"This marketplace does accord advantages to first movers," Osaka said in a joint conference call with news media.

Kathleen Earley, AT&T vice president of network commerce services, said the alliance aims to extend the reputation for reliability of its global networks with HP's capabilities in supplying and managing computer systems for large customers.
The partners said they would collaborate with iCat Corp. and other electronic commerce software developers to help merchants process and fulfil customer orders.
Analysts said the alliance was the latest in a series of accords aimed at boosting Internet commerce.

"It's part of an ongoing campaign for HP to use some forcefulness in carving out a prominent position as the major proponent of electronic commerce," said Daniel Kunstler, an analyst who covers the computer industry at JP Morgan.

HP stock hit a new high of $65.25, and closed up $3.675 at $65.0625 on the New York Stock Exchange, with analysts saying the stock was catching up with a rally in other computer industry shares. AT&T stock rose 19 cents to $35.31 on the NYSE.

"Our view is you can't go it alone," Osaka said. "You need to leverage the streth of key partners like AT&T. ... We want to be the owner of the new model, dominate the model and sign up as much of (HP's distribution) channel as we can."
